speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you presented with an episode of loss of consciousness; to ensure your safety, please remain seated while I ask you some questions. How long were you unconscious, and did anyone witness the event or notice any shaking or jerking movements?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Vasovagal Syncope (Micturition Syncope).

Thank you for that detail; losing consciousness immediately after urination is a classic presentation of this condition. Given the brief duration and rapid recovery without confusion, this supports a reflex mechanism rather than a cardiac arrhythmia. Are you currently experiencing any chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath? REQUEST TEST: ECG.
